nary_nodes.label: Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs
evidence: Microsoft has announced it has cut 4,800 jobs

nary_nodes.label: 2.1% of workforce cut
evidence: roughly 2.1% of its workforce

nary_nodes.label: Xbox axes 1,600 roles immediately
evidence: more than 1,600 roles immediately axed at Xbox

nary_nodes.label: Xbox begins significant restructure
evidence: beginning the most significant restructure in Xbox history

nary_nodes.label: Four Xbox studios spun off
evidence: Four Xbox game development studios - Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory and Undead Lab - would also be spun off as part of the changes

nary_nodes.label: Additional 1,600 roles reduced from Xbox
evidence: Another 1,600 roles will be reduced from Xbox as a result.

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft needs to focus on customer-delivering areas
evidence: Amy Coleman, executive vice president at Microsoft, told employees in a memo that the tech giant needed to focus on areas that can deliver for customers amid a "fast-changing industry".

nary_nodes.label: Xbox restructure is most significant in history
evidence: Asha Sharma, who recently took over as Xbox's chief executive, said in a note to staff it was "beginning the most significant restructure in Xbox history".

nary_nodes.label: Changes are for a bigger future for Xbox
evidence: "These changes are about a bigger future for Xbox, not a smaller one," Sharma said in a note, shared on X.

nary_nodes.label: Companies must change with industry
evidence: "Companies don't get to choose whether their industry changes; they only get to choose whether they change with it," she said.

nary_nodes.label: AI changing how work gets done
evidence: She noted that while the company would not replace the lost roles with AI, "what is true is that AI is changing how work gets done".

nary_nodes.label: Gaming industry experiencing difficult times
evidence: already difficult time in the gaming industry, with many studios still reeling from brutal layoffs in recent years.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox culled 2,000 staff and shuttered studios
evidence: In 2024, Xbox culled more than 2,000 staff and shuttered four studios

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft cut up to 9,000 jobs
evidence: Microsoft said it would cut up to 9,000 jobs after setting out plans to double down on its multi-billion-dollar AI spending.

nary_nodes.label: Firms hiked hardware prices
evidence: The spiralling costs of hardware have also prompted firms including Microsoft to hike the price of years-old consoles and similar consumer gadgets

nary_nodes.label: Spiralling costs of hardware
evidence: The spiralling costs of hardware

nary_nodes.label: AI data centres blamed for pushing demand
evidence: many blaming AI data centres for pushing up demand too quickly for supply to catch up.

nary_nodes.label: Reset needed across Xbox
evidence: Sharma said on Monday that while she knew the cuts were "painful", there was a "reset" needed across Xbox's entire content portfolio, platform and operations.

nary_nodes.label: Changes mark a major reset for Xbox
evidence: Tech analyst Paolo Pescatore told the BBC the changes indeed marked a "major reset" for the company

nary_nodes.label: Challenge to define Xbox's stand
evidence: "The challenge is not just cutting costs; it is defining what Xbox stands for in a world where games are moving across console, PC, cloud and subscription platforms," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Mojang and King report directly to Sharma
evidence: Mojang and Candy Crush developer King will now report directly to Sharma.

nary_nodes.label: Restructuring underlines Xbox's vision
evidence: Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere Analysis said this restructuring "underlines Xbox's vision for its studios and content, which will be more heavily focused on the biggest IP and audiences".

nary_nodes.label: Company previously bought studios for Game Pass
evidence: He said the company had previously bought a plethora of studios to boost offerings on its subscription service Game Pass.

nary_nodes.label: Some teams/games better suited outside Xbox
evidence: "But the company has now decided that some of these teams and the games they are building would be better suited to sit outside the Xbox organisation," he said

nary_nodes.label: Decision not to close studios is positive
evidence: adding that its decision not close them was "positive news during a difficult time".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine and Compulsion return to independent management
evidence: Double Fine and Compulsion will both return to independent management.

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft acquired Double Fine
evidence: Double Fine, acquired by Microsoft in 2019

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine thankful to Xbox
evidence: Double Fine, acquired by Microsoft in 2019, wrote on X that it was "thankful to everyone at Xbox for seven great years together".

nary_nodes.label: Grateful for outcome preserving history and culture
evidence: The Psychonauts developer added it was grateful to have been able to reach an outcome "which preserves our history and culture, and returns ownership of our games to us".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine and Compulsion depart with IP
evidence: Both itself and Compulsion, which developed action-adventure title South of Midnight, will depart with their intellectual property (IP).

nary_nodes.label: Compulsion's immediate priority is team support
evidence: "Our immediate priority is to support our team throughout this transition period," Compulsion said on X

nary_nodes.label: Compulsion confident in its future
evidence: adding it was confident in its future.
